note: Shahpur 3-4 row prints 1,842 | 921 | 921 | 921 | 921 | ... (all unmarried); identical values are real.
Alayet prints 1 house, 15 persons, 15 males, females '...', 15 Buddhist, 15 Burmese, 12 in the next education column; an all-male village of 15, so the identical values are real.
0-5 Unmarried column prints 1,000 in nearly every row (999 in rows 4, 8, 9 and 26, 998 in row 29), matching the transcription. Almost all infant females are unmarried.

Both 'age' and 'district' columns hold the city serial number 1-23. The print repeats the serial number at the edges of the spread (Serial number column 1), so the duplication is real; these are row-label columns, not data.
Brahmin Males Infant row prints 2,678 in all five columns (Actual, <=3, Intermediate, <=5, Final); the infant figure is not smoothed.
Brahmin Females Infant row (p.182) prints 3,675 in all five columns; the infant figure is carried unchanged through the adjustment.

The print has no Race males/females columns: Race is a text entry (Burmese / Talaing / Karen (Sgau)). The Race and Religion sex columns in the transcription are both copies of Population males/females, often swapped. Religion is printed as per-religion counts (e.g. Buddhist: Kamun 286, Titan 205, Thayagon 169, Yitkangale 124, Paukkongale 26, Tenan 420, Gwaywa 92, Zwepa 332, Paingkyon 1312), not by sex. No printed values exist for this column.
Same as id 0: the print has no Race females (or Religion females) column. Both are invented copies of Population females/males. No printed values exist for this column.

Gwaywa prints houses 21, persons 92, males 46, females 46 (so the Population 46/46 is genuine). Religion prints Buddhist 92 and Race prints Burmese; the Religion/Race males/females cells are not printed and are copies. Only the Population cells are given.
Sikhs 1-2 row prints 224 | 112 | 112 | 112 | 112 | ... (all unmarried, equal sexes); identical values are real.

Col 9 (60+ per 100 aged 15-40, 1931 Female) prints 11, 11, 11, 12, 11, 9 for Baroda State, City, Central Gujarat, Kathiawad, North Gujarat, South Gujarat, matching the transcription. Side note: the transcribed rows are the upper Subsidiary Table V (natural divisions), not V-A (by religion) as the title says.
Table V A col 10 (1921 Males) prints 10,10,10,10 (State) / 10,10,10,10 (Lowland) / 11,11,10,10 (Midland) / 7,7,6,8 (Highland), matching the transcription; these proportions really are mostly 10.
Table V A col 12 (1911 Males) prints 10,10,10,10 / 10,10,9,10 / 11,11,10,10 / 8,8,7,10, matching the transcription.

This page (p.109, right half of the spread) prints only columns 11-23 (Hindi/Urdu, Other languages, Total literate, Total illiterate, Literate in English). There is no serial, age or district column. Both 'States. | age' and 'States. | district' are row indices 1-36 added by the transcription, so they hold no printed values and should be dropped. The row names (states) are on the facing page, which is not shown.
